# Set up the stage

I'm trying now to code contrasts with the following structure:

-   contrasts as ratios

-   nested contrasts as differences between contrasts

I start by erasing all the environment and reloading my datasets.

```{r}
rm(list = ls())
load("~/Documents/Github/RelativeSize/3_results/environments/after_ds.RData")
```

Then, let's set up the stage.

```{r define-parameters-metaecos-biomass}

# --- DEFINE PARAMETERS --- #

response_variable_selected = "bioarea_mm2_per_ml"
```

Figure 2. Time series of biomass at the meta-ecosystem level. Left panels show fixed volume disturbance effects (red), while right panels show volume disturbance relative to size (yellow) across four different disturbance volumes (6.43, 9, 15, and 45 ml). Solid lines represent connected meta-ecosystems, and dashed lines represent unconnected meta-ecosystems. Points represent means and error bars indicate 95 % confidence intervals. Vertical grey lines are disturbance events. To reduce overlapping, data points were slightly jittered along the x axis. The grey shading shows periods before the initial disturbance and resource flow, which were excluded from the analysis.

</details>

<details>

<summary>Prepare & plot data for analysis</summary>

```{r prepare-data-for-analysis-metaecos}

# --- PREPARE DATA FOR ANALYSIS --- #

# Add baselines

baseline = ds_metaecosystems %>%
  filter(time_point == time_point_of_baselines) %>%
  select(metaecosystem_ID,
         all_of(response_variable_selected)) %>%
  rename(baseline = all_of(response_variable_selected))

data_for_analysis = ds_metaecosystems %>%
  left_join(baseline)

# Filter and mutate

data_for_analysis = data_for_analysis %>%
  filter(time_point %in% time_points_model,
         !is.na(!!sym(response_variable_selected)),
         connection == "connected" | 
          ecosystems_combined %in% unconnected_metaecosystems_selected) %>%
  mutate(conn = factor(x = ifelse(connection == "connected", 
                                  "con", 
                                  "unconnected"),
                       levels = c("unconnected", "con")))
```

```{r plot-data-for-analysis-metaecos, fig.height = figures_height_rmd_output, fig.width = figures_height_rmd_output}

# --- PLOT ONE PLOT PER ECOSYSTEM SIZE --- #

plot.metaecos.sizes.one.by.one.means(data_for_analysis,
                                     response_variable_selected,
                                     y_upper_limit = 25)
```

</details>

<details>

<summary>Create model</summary>

```{r create-model-metaecos}

# --- CREATE MODEL --- #

# Prepare data

data_for_analysis = data_for_analysis %>% 
  rename(size = ecosystem_size_ml,
         disturb_type = volume_disturbed_across_sizes) %>%
  mutate(size = as.factor(size),
         day = as.factor(day))

# Define formula

formula = as.formula(paste("bioarea_mm2_per_ml ~",
                           "size * conn * disturb_type +",
                           "(1 | time_point) +",
                           "(1 | baseline)")) %>%
  print()

# Create model 

model <- glmmTMB(formula,
                 data = data_for_analysis,
                 family = tweedie(link = "log"),
                 dispformula = ~ bioarea_mm2_per_ml)
car::Anova(model, type = "III")
```

```{r show-model-summary}

# --- SHOW MODEL SUMMARY --- #

print(summary(model), digits = 3)
```

# Look into the marginal means

Now we want to have marginal means that are back transformed.

This is the one with the log.

```{r}
# --- CODE MODEL CONSTRASTS --- #

# Estimate marginal means (least-squares means)

emmeans_output = emmeans(model,
                         specs = ~  conn * disturb_type * size,
                         adjust = "sidak",
                         lmer.df = "satterthwaite") 

emmeans_output
```

This is the on with the back transformation.

```{r}
# --- CODE MODEL CONSTRASTS --- #

# Estimate marginal means (least-squares means)

emmeans_output = emmeans(model,
                         specs = ~  conn * disturb_type * size,
                         adjust = "sidak",
                         lmer.df = "satterthwaite",
                         type = "response") 

emmeans_output
```

Good.

# Look into the contrasts

Let's now try to get contrasts which are based on ratios and not on differences of absolute values.

These are with the absolute values.

```{r}
# Compute the contrasts

contrasts = contrast(emmeans_output, 
                     method = list("6.43 ml fixed" = con_fixed_6_43 - uncon_fixed_6_43,
                                   "9.00 ml fixed" = con_fixed_9 - uncon_fixed_9,
                                   "15.00 ml fixed" = con_fixed_15 - uncon_fixed_15,
                                   "45.00 ml fixed" = con_fixed_45 - uncon_fixed_45,
                                   "6.43 ml relative" = con_relative_6_43 - uncon_relative_6_43,
                                   "9.00 ml relative" = con_relative_9 - uncon_relative_9,
                                   "15.00 ml relative" = con_relative_15 - uncon_relative_15,
                                   "45.00 ml relative" = con_relative_45 - uncon_relative_45))
```
